topic_name: The Structure, Typology and Sociodynamics of Culture

51.question: Why can the structure of culture be described on several bases?

options.A: Each sphere of culture has its own unchanging bearer
options.B: The bases of classification coincide with periods of political history
options.C: The units of culture replace one another in sequence without overlapping
options.D: The elements of culture are interconnected but allow grouping by different criteria
options.E: The sources of cultural creativity are determined by a single territorial feature

52.question: The distinction between folk culture and professional culture is based on the criterion of...

options.A: The territory of distribution
options.B: Age affiliation
options.C: The source of formation
options.D: Historical duration
options.E: Geographical scale

53.question: The features that distinguish folk culture from professional culture in terms of the source of creation:

options.A: Specialized training as a condition of creation
options.B: Legal protection of the integrity of the original
options.C: Fixed personal authorship
options.D: Modification of the model in transmission between generations
options.E: Collective anonymity

54.question: The combination of features that characterizes professional culture in terms of the source of creation is...

options.A: Collective anonymity and free modification
options.B: Oral transmission and the absence of copyright
options.C: Special training and fixed authorship
options.D: Inherited status and territorial isolation
options.E: Age homogeneity and everyday purpose

55.question: How are the general culture and the professional culture of a particular person related?

options.A: Professional culture constitutes the highest level of general culture
options.B: The two cultures differ only in the amount of information acquired
options.C: General culture arises after professional training is completed
options.D: Professional mastery does not guarantee a general cultural development
options.E: General culture is determined by the sum of specialized professional knowledge

56.question: The emergence of professional culture is associated with...

options.A: The disappearance of oral folk creativity
options.B: The unification of all regional traditions
options.C: The cessation of the transmission of experience between generations
options.D: The emergence of mass electronic broadcasting
options.E: The division of mental and physical labour

57.question: The thesis that the structure of education depends on the logic of the structure of culture belongs to...

options.A: A. Ya. Flier
options.B: V. A. Konev
options.C: V. S. Bibler
options.D: M. S. Kagan
options.E: E. S. Markaryan

58.question: The thesis that the structure of education is a "tracing" of culture illustrates...

options.A: The independence of pedagogical organization from the historical type of society
options.B: The absence of differences between teaching and the inheritance of instincts
options.C: The universality of a single educational form for all eras
options.D: The origin of professional art in the school timetable
options.E: The link between the class-and-lesson system and the branch-based structure of modern culture

59.question: A ritual object has kept its form but has become a museum exhibit. What has changed from the standpoint of the functional approach?

options.A: Only its geographical origin
options.B: Its cultural function, and with it the status of the object in the system of culture
options.C: Its archaeological dating
options.D: Only the physical mass of the object
options.E: Necessarily the material it is made of

60.question: The study of the hierarchy of what is significant in various spheres of human activity belongs to the ... approach.

options.A: Biographical
options.B: Energetic
options.C: Axiological
options.D: Diffusionist
options.E: Technological

61.question: Which research principle does NOT correspond to the structural approach to culture?

options.A: Studying the stable organization of cultural messages
options.B: Identifying the recurring elements of cultural texts
options.C: Searching for the hidden logic of relations between elements
options.D: Comparative analysis of the structure of sign systems
options.E: Explaining cultural differences exclusively by the age of the cultural organism

62.question: The primacy of material production in explaining cultural evolution is asserted by the ... approach.

options.A: Symbolic
options.B: Idealist
options.C: Ludic (play-based)
options.D: Materialist
options.E: Transcendentalist

63.question: The subject matter of the sociodynamics of culture comprises...

options.A: The distribution of stable cultural forms among bearers and scales
options.B: Changes in culture and in the human being under the action of internal and external forces
options.C: The relations between the sign, the object it denotes and the interpreter
options.D: The structure of the system of spiritual values at a given historical moment
options.E: The rules for combining signs within a particular language of culture

64.question: Why can cultural dynamics not be identified with progress alone?

options.A: Progress describes results, while dynamics describes exclusively the intentions of authors
options.B: Progress denotes borrowings, while dynamics denotes only internal innovations
options.C: Cultural dynamics includes both ascending and regressive lines
options.D: Dynamics covers only brief changes within a single generation
options.E: Progress relates to spiritual culture, while dynamics relates to material culture

65.question: For the life processes of groups and individuals, the following time scale is applied...

options.A: Medium-scale: 1-25 years
options.B: Micro-scale: 48-55 years
options.C: Macro-scale: 25-30 years
options.D: Micro-scale: 1-25 years
options.E: Medium-scale: 100 years or more

66.question: Indicate the processes assigned to medium-scale dynamics.

options.A: Economic fluctuations over 48-55 years
options.B: A change in the norms of a small group over 5 years
options.C: A change of social formations over several centuries
options.D: A change of generations over 25-30 years
options.E: The transformation of a language over several centuries

67.question: For studying the transformations of a language over centuries, the ... scale is applied.

options.A: Situational
options.B: Micro-scale
options.C: Medium-scale
options.D: Biographical
options.E: Macro-scale

68.question: The author of the work "Culture and Explosion" is...

options.A: A. Losev
options.B: Yu. Lotman
options.C: M. Bakhtin
options.D: G. Shpet
options.E: V. Bibler

69.question: The distinguishing feature of the "moment of explosion" in Lotman's description is...

options.A: A single outcome, predetermined by the entire prehistory
options.B: The complete cessation of gradual processes
options.C: The presence of several possible transitions, of which only one is realized
options.D: The absence of any cultural consequences of the event
options.E: The repetition of an already realized trajectory without alternatives

70.question: The pair of processes that illustrates the difference between explosive and gradual dynamics:

options.A: The copying of a text and the original discovery of an idea
options.B: The legal registration and archival storage of a document
options.C: The preservation of a custom and the mechanical copying of a custom
options.D: Technical realization and a subsequent scientific discovery
options.E: The emergence of a scientific idea and its technical realization

71.question: The propositions that correspond to the understanding of a cultural crisis:

options.A: A crisis can have positive cultural consequences
options.B: A systemic crisis requires the same pace of change in all subsystems
options.C: Simultaneous deformations of subsystems may make a crisis systemic
options.D: The positive role of a crisis excludes the disintegration of old normative structures
options.E: A crisis is defined exclusively by a decrease in the volume of cultural production

72.question: The introduction of norms and objects already tested by another culture is called...

options.A: Innovative and exploratory activity
options.B: Cultural isolation
options.C: Stylistic mummification
options.D: Cultural borrowing
options.E: Archetypal compensation

73.question: A deliberate departure from established norms in favour of new models of activity belongs to...

options.A: Normative codification
options.B: Innovative and exploratory activity
options.C: Passive transmission of tradition
options.D: Ritual reproduction
options.E: Archival conservation

74.question: In a real cultural process, the dying out of old norms and the introduction of new ones are related as follows...

options.A: They depend exclusively on external borrowings
options.B: They always occur at the same pace
options.C: They exclude simultaneity within one society
options.D: They are always separated by a long period of normlessness
options.E: They may proceed in parallel and at different speeds

75.question: P. Sorokin considers the following directions of the movement of cultural values:

options.A: Only from the metropolis to the dependent periphery
options.B: Between social strata
options.C: Only from professional authors to folklore performers
options.D: Only within a single ethnically closed territory
options.E: Between countries and regions
